A high wave hits ashore in Keelung, northern Taiwan on Thursday (October 22, 2026), as typhoon Champi approaches the area. | Photo Credit: AP
Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday (October 23, 2026) ahead of ​the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast ‌to bring strong winds and torrential ​rain, though the storm is ⁠weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island.
At one point a super ‌typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this ‌year, Champi was still packing ‌gusts ⁠of around 191 kph (119 mph) near its ⁠centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).
The storm was about 330 km (205 miles) east of Taiwan's southern ​tip, the CWA ‌said. The storm's forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and ‌eventually move into southern Japan.
The administration ​said its radius was around 320 km (200 miles), large enough to ⁠cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two ‌days.
Taiwan's financial markets will also close for Friday (October 23), while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal.
The Transport Ministry said all 262 domestic ‌flights were cancelled for Friday (October 23), along with more ​than 350 international ones.
Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps ⁠casualties low. Although more common in summer, ⁠the storms can strike in autumn, bringing strong winds and torrential rain.
The ‌typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan's westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, ​in Okinawa Prefecture.
